title: Cutoff-spline admission: fractional priority braking for smooth tenant load-shedding
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional overloads and cross-region failovers we currently rely on hard cutoff and tiered token-bucket admission policies which produce sharp capacity cliffs and sudden request failures for selected tenants. This causes bursty error rates and violates tail SLOs for high-priority customers.

Goal: Implement a new admission controller mode called "cutoff-spline" that applies fractional priority braking — a smooth, continuous reduction of accepted query rate per tenant using a spline-based admission curve instead of discrete tiers. The controller should integrate signals from circuit breakers, SLO credit depletion, and regional capacity windows to produce gradual degradation (response trimming, reduced top-k, model fallback) rather than abrupt rejection.

Scope: Runtime admission controller + operator config + Console visualization + rollout plan. This ticket covers design, prototype, integration tests, and canary rollout for hosted+dedicated fleets. Private deployments will be provided config compatibility docs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cutoff-spline admission controller implemented in runtime path and feature-flagged.
- Controller exposes per-tenant braking_curve and current_braking_fraction metrics.
- Integration tests that simulate regional capacity drop show >30% reduction in tail spikes vs hard-cutoff baseline.
- Console shows a per-tenant curve editor and live visualization in the Rollouts dashboard.
- Canary rollout plan executed on one hosted region with monitoring and rollback playbook.
- Documentation (Confluence) and a runbook entry added for on-call playbook.
design_decisions:
- Use cubic Hermite spline interpolation (monotonic-preserving) to map tenant priority score -> accepted rate fraction. This avoids oscillation while keeping operator control.
- Priority score is derived from (tenant_tier weight, active_slo_credits, recent_error_budget_burn, regional_penalty_factor). We normalize to [0,1].
- Braking fraction multiplies the tenant's token-bucket allocation; admission uses probabilistic accept with seed derived from request id to keep partial acceptance deterministic per request.
- When braking_fraction < 0.2, trigger graceful degradation pipeline (response trimming / nucleus sampling temp increase / model fall back) instead of immediate rejection.
- Circuit-breaker OPEN or severe backlog forces spline to the lower envelope but preserves a minimum reserve for P0 clients configured in tenant metadata.
implementation_plan:
1) Add new AdmissionStrategy interface and implement CutoffSplineStrategy in runtime (C++/Rust module).
2) Metrics: braking_fraction_gauge, braking_curve_version, accepted_rate_delta, spline_evaluation_latency.
3) Expose strategy config in operator API and Console with curve editor (control points).
4) Add deterministic probabilistic accept helper and integrate with existing token-bucket code path.
5) Add fallback triggers for graceful degradation modes.
6) Write integration tests simulating multi-region failover and circuit-breaker flips.
7) Create canary pipeline and smoke-test job.

Owners: Miguel (implementation), Leila (metrics + dashboard), Noah (console), Asha (design + runbook).
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: Per-tenant braking_fraction heatmap, regional aggregate accepted_rate, SLO burn vs expected with/without spline.
- Alerts: >10% divergence between expected accepted_rate and observed for >5m; braking_curve_eval_latency P50>10ms; canary error-rate increase >2x baseline for 15m.
- On-call playbook links to runbook: Confluence - Cutoff Spline Playbook (link below).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for spline math covering edge cases (flat sections, steep slopes, boundary clamping).
- Deterministic probabilistic acceptance tests to ensure reproducible behavior across retries.
- Chaos tests: simulated region failure + gradual capacity loss with load generator (k6) comparing hard-cutoff vs spline.
- Load test to verify no regression in p50/p95 latency under typical traffic.
- Canary validation harness that gates rollout on predefined metrics.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag.
2) Canary in region-us-west-2 on a subset of hosted fleet (5% tenants) for 24h.
3) Expand to dedicated blue pool with low-impact tenants (48h).
4) Global ramp to 25% regions, monitor for two days.
4b) If circuit-breaker interactions observed, revert to feature-flag off immediately.
5) Full rollout with operator training and Console guide.
6) For Private deployments, ship config schema and an operator migration guide with example curve presets.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Spline misconfiguration could overly throttle high-value tenants. Mitigation: minimum reserve config per tenant, automated safety checks comparing pre/post accepted_rate.
- Risk: Added eval latency could increase request tail. Mitigation: ensure spline eval path is optimized (precompile piecewise coefficients) and instrumented; fallback to cached braking_fraction if eval > 5ms.
- Risk: Interaction with existing circuit-breaker triggers may oscillate. Mitigation: add hysteresis and low-pass filter to inputs (SLO burn, backlog).
notes: Prototype math and charts available in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Cutoff+Spline+Admission
